# 解深密經疏

**ID:** X0369
**Volume:** X21
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 大小乘釋經部／方等部疏
**Byline:** 唐 圓測撰
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 618–907
**Juans:** 9
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X0369

## Contributors
- 圓測 (A001414)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

X369 in nine fascicles (originally ten) is the principal Chinese-language commentary on *[the Jiě shēnmì jīng 解深密經](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0353)* (T676), composed by the Silla-born Yogācāra master [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC) (613–696), the senior of [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s two principal Chinese disciples and founder of the *Xīmíng* 西明 sub-school of Fǎxiàng / Cí'ēn Yogācāra. The text-block heading lists the commentary's chapter-by-chapter table of contents matching [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s eight chapters of T676. Composed at Xīmíngsì 西明寺 in Cháng'ān between [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s 647 translation of the parent sūtra and [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC)'s death in 696.

**Abstract**

[圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC)'s commentary is the single most influential medieval exposition of the *Saṃdhinirmocana* and one of the most consequential works of Tang Yogācāra. It is preserved in the Chinese tradition only fragmentarily — fascicles 1–8 plus part of fascicle 10 (the commentary on the eighth and final chapter, *Rúlái chéngsuǒzuò shì pǐn* 如來成所作事品) — but the work survives complete in Tibetan translation as *Dgongs pa nges par 'grel pa'i rgya cher 'grel pa* (D 4016 / P 5517), commissioned by the Tibetan emperor Khri Srong-lde-btsan in the late eighth century. The Tibetan version was retro-translated into Chinese in the early twentieth century by Guānkōng 觀空 (1903–1989) to recover the missing fascicle 9. [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC)'s commentary is celebrated for two distinctive features: (1) its philological rigour, citing all four Chinese versions of the *Saṃdhinirmocana* ([KR6i0352](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0352), [KR6i0353](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0353), [KR6i0355](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0355), [KR6i0356](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0356)) plus an acquaintance with Sanskrit terminology that probably came from [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s translation atelier; (2) its ecumenical engagement with rival exegeses, especially that of [Kuījī](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) / Cí'ēn 慈恩 (632–682) and the Yogācāra-bhūmi tradition, sometimes against the more rigid line of the orthodox Cí'ēn school. After [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC)'s death, [Kuījī](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA)'s heirs charged [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC) with "stealing" [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s lectures, and his works were partly suppressed in Cháng'ān. The commentary became foundational for Korean (Silla / Goryeo) and Japanese Hossō / Yogācāra exegesis. The composition window given here brackets [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC)'s mature scholarly career in Cháng'ān.

Related canonical texts: parent sūtra [KR6i0353](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0353) (T676); related recensions [KR6i0352](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0352) (T675), [KR6i0355](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0355) (T677), [KR6i0356](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0356) (T678), [KR6i0357](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0357) (T679).
